references.text: The same chapter describes similar cleansing rituals for the one who let the goat go to Azazel, involving washing of clothes and body before returning to the camp.
The preceding verses describe the sin offering goat and bull that are to be burned outside the camp, which verse 28 follows up with a cleansing requirement for the one who burns them.
Describes how the sin offering bull is to be burned outside the camp, the same practice as in the Day of Atonement ritual.
Refers to washing clothes and vessels that have been in contact with the flesh of the sin offering, as part of the cleansing practice.
A general cleansing regulation requiring washing of clothes upon contact with unclean things.
Regulation to wash clothes and bathe in water as part of the cleansing ritual.
Similar cleansing requirements for the one who burns the red heifer – washing of clothes and body, unclean until evening.
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to the sin offerings that were burned outside the camp, linking this to Jesus' suffering outside the city gate.
